Why your photo keeps getting rejected

The real reasons exam portals reject a photo upload, in the order they actually happen, and how to fix each one.

The error message is rarely honest

Portals test several conditions and report one generic failure. You get told the upload was unsuccessful, or that the file is invalid, with no indication of which check tripped. That is why people try the same fix five times.

Work through the causes below in order. They are arranged by how often they turn out to be the culprit, not by how obvious they seem.

One: the file is under the minimum

This is the single most common cause and the most counter-intuitive, because the person has been actively trying to make the file smaller. Re-read the notification. If it specifies a range, you have a floor as well as a ceiling.

Two: the photo is sideways

Phone cameras do not rotate the image when you turn the handset. They record the orientation in a small tag inside the file and leave the pixels where they are. Your gallery app reads that tag and shows the photo the right way up, so everything looks fine.

Plenty of upload systems ignore the tag. The portal receives what the sensor actually captured, which is rotated ninety degrees, and either rejects it or accepts a sideways photo onto your admit card. Any tool that reads orientation properly fixes this silently, ours included.

Advertisement

Three: the dimensions are close but not exact

Some portals accept a range of dimensions and some demand an exact match. If yours wants exactly 200 by 230 pixels, then 201 by 230 fails. Resizing by dragging a corner in a phone gallery app almost never lands on an exact number, because it preserves the aspect ratio and rounds.

Four: wrong format, or a format pretending to be another

Most forms want JPG. Renaming a PNG to end in .jpg does not convert it. The bytes inside still identify it as a PNG and any competent server checks those bytes rather than trusting the extension. You need a genuine re-encode, which is what a resizer does when it hands you a JPG.

Watch for HEIC as well. Newer iPhones save in HEIC by default, and almost no Indian exam portal accepts it. In iOS, Settings, Camera, Formats, choose Most Compatible to shoot JPG instead.

Five: the file name

Some older portals choke on spaces, apostrophes, brackets or non-English characters in a file name. If everything else looks right, rename the file to something plain like photo.jpg and try again. It costs nothing to rule out.

Six: the background is too dark or too busy

A few portals run an automated contrast check, especially on signatures. Paper photographed in room light reads as grey rather than white and can fail. Shoot in daylight, avoid casting a shadow across the page, and use a whitening option if your tool offers one.

If none of that works

Try a different browser. Portals under heavy load during the final days of an application window sometimes fail in ways that have nothing to do with your file. Trying at a quieter hour solves more problems than it should.

Do not leave it until the last day. The servers are at their worst exactly when everyone is trying to submit, and a genuine portal fault at that point leaves you no time to work around it.
